THE SHAPE OF THIS TALK

Four questions we will answer about every method

Each algorithm gets the same four-part treatment, so the comparison between them is structural rather than anecdotal. The methods that were state of the art get a fifth question.

1

What could the previous method not do?

Every innovation in this field was a response to a named, measured failure — usually named by the paper that fixed it, which is what makes this timeline evidenced rather than imposed.

2

What changed technically?

The algorithmic change: a different prior, a different training target, a different operator. Stated precisely enough that you could implement it.

3

Which line of code changed?

A Before → After from the reference implementations. Contribution → algorithmic change → implementation change → measured improvement, as one chain.

4

What did it buy, and what did it cost?

The measured improvement, the applications it opened, and the new limitation it created — because every step in this story created the next problem.

And for the SOTA methods, a fifth: what made it state of the art, on which benchmark and in which years, and why it did not make the others obsolete.

THE PROBLEM

One equation, three unknowns, eighteen years

Given only y, infinitely many splits into x + v are arithmetically valid. Every method in this talk supplies the missing information in a different way — that supplied information is called the prior, and the whole story is about where it lives.

y — what the sensor produced · x — the clean image we want · v — the noise
  • The classical answer writes the prior down as a formula: minimise ½‖y − x‖² + λ·Φ(x). You can read Φ, differentiate it, and argue about it.
  • The deep answer replaces Φ with a tensor of learned weights. You cannot read it, but you can download it and it runs in 60 ms.
  • The self-supervised answer takes the prior partly from the test image itself, so no clean data is needed at all.
  • Where the prior lives, and who writes it, is the single axis this whole talk runs along.
DnCNN17 §I · standard MAP formulation

GROUND RULES

What 'state of the art' means in this talk

The phrase is used loosely in most presentations. We use it with three qualifiers attached, because that is what makes the SOTA comparison later in the talk meaningful rather than rhetorical.

A SOTA claim needs three things

  • A benchmark and a metric. 'Best denoiser' is meaningless. 'Highest PSNR on BSD68 at σ=25' is a claim you can check.
  • A comparison protocol. Two papers reporting on the same dataset can still disagree, so wherever a row compares two methods we take both numbers from one table.
  • Honesty about what is not reported. No paper here states how long it held a position, so this talk does not claim SOTA windows — only the publication date and which table each method leads.

Which is why there is no single winner

  • Different benchmarks measure different capabilities: BSD68 measures average-case Gaussian removal, Urban100 measures long-range self-similarity, SIDD measures real sensor noise.
  • A method can lead one and trail another. Restormer, NAFNet and MambaIR each lead a different table today.
  • We return to this on slide 36 with the numbers, because 'why are there several SOTAs' is the question this talk is built to answer.
reading, grounded in the benchmark definitions used by DnCNN17, Restormer22, NAFNet22

CLASSICAL DIP
BM3D · 2007 · THE BASELINE

The innovation: filter patches together, not alone

Dabov et al., IEEE TIP 2007. Previous transform-domain methods shrank each patch independently. BM3D's innovation is to group similar patches first, creating a third axis along which the signal is nearly constant and the noise is not.

Block matching in practice: the reference patch R and the similar patches BM3D groups with it before collaborative 3-D filtering. [BM3D07 · Fig. 2]
1
What changed
Block-match similar patches into a 3-D stack, transform the stack, hard-threshold, invert, aggregate — then repeat using the cleaner estimate as a Wiener pilot.
2
Why it works
The paper's own ablation: even a transform that is random apart from the DC loses only 0.1–0.4 dB. The grouping does the work, not the transform. [BM3D07 §V]
3
Impact
BSD68 σ=25: 28.57 dB at 2.85 s per 512×512. Became the reference line every paper for a decade had to beat.
4
Still in use
Appears as a live baseline in Noise2Noise (2018), Noise2Void (2019), ZS-N2N (2023) and Restormer (2022) — a seventeen-year-old algorithm is still what new zero-shot methods must beat, because it needs no training data.
5
Applications
The zero-shot comparison in those same papers, and the fallback where there is neither training data nor a GPU. On real sensor noise it still beats an AWGN-trained DnCNN by 1.99 dB. [Restormer22 Table 6]
BM3D07 §II-C, §V · DnCNN17 Table II, Table IV · baselines in N2N18, N2V19, ZS-N2N23

CLASSICAL DIP
WNNM · 2014 · BEFORE → AFTER

WNNM vs BM3D — the same grouping, a better estimator

Gu et al., CVPR 2014. WNNM keeps BM3D's non-local grouping and replaces what happens to the group. This is the first clean Before → After in the story, and it is entirely inside one step.

Aspect BM3D (2007) WNNM (2014) Why it matters
Core algorithm Group patches, shrink in a 3-D transform Group patches, recover a low-rank matrix Stacked near-copies are low rank by construction — a stronger structural assumption
Key innovation Collaborative hard-thresholding Weighted nuclear norm: wᵢ ∝ 1⁄σᵢ Large singular values carry the image and are shrunk less; standard NNM shrinks all equally
Implementation change 3-D DCT + threshold SVD per patch group + per-value shrinkage, iterated One transform call becomes an iterated SVD — the entire cost difference
Performance 28.57 dB · 2.85 s 28.83 dB · 773.2 s +0.26 dB for a 271× slowdown
Limitation Fixed hand-set parameters Non-convex; still per-image optimisation Neither can reuse anything learned from one image on the next
Applications General-purpose, real-time-ish Offline / quality-critical restoration The cost makes WNNM impractical for interactive or batch use
This row is the whole argument for what comes next. Seven years of hand-designed priors bought 0.26 dB on BSD68 at σ=25, and the best method became 271× slower than the second best. The era had hit a wall in quality and cost simultaneously.
DnCNN17 Table II, Table IV · WNNM14 §3, Theorem 2

CLASSICAL DIP
BOTTLENECK 1

Why the era ended — stated by the paper that ended it

DnCNN's introduction names the classical era's drawbacks in its own words. Quoting the paper that broke the bottleneck, rather than asserting it ourselves, is what makes this an evidenced timeline.

DRAWBACK 1

The prior is paid for once per image

Prior-based methods involve a complex optimization problem in the testing stage. Nothing learned on image 1 helps image 2. WNNM: 773 s, every time. [DnCNN17 §I]

DRAWBACK 2

The prior is written by hand

The models are generally non-convex and involve several manually chosen parameters — block size, thresholds, λ, different values above and below σ=40. [DnCNN17 §I]

DRAWBACK 3

Its form limits the ceiling

Performance is inherently restricted to the specified forms of prior. You cannot exceed what your formula can express, however well you tune it. [DnCNN17 §I]

DRAWBACK 4

One model per noise level

Bridge methods train a specific model for a certain noise level and are limited in blind image denoising. In a real camera, σ is never known. [DnCNN17 §I]

DnCNN17 §I — all four quoted from the paper's introduction

THE BRIDGE
TNRD · 2016 · BEFORE → AFTER

Unrolling — the step that made the transition continuous

Chen & Pock, TPAMI. Worth ninety seconds because it is the conceptual bridge: it shows that a classical optimiser and a neural network are the same object viewed differently, which is why the move to deep learning was not a rupture.

The diffusion network unrolled as a feed-forward graph: learned filters, trainable nonlinearity and reaction force applied at every stage. [TNRD16/17 · Fig. 1]
Aspect Classical optimiser TNRD (unrolled) Why it matters
Iteration count Run to convergence, unbounded Truncated to a fixed K (usually < 10) Runtime becomes a constant — the first half of bottleneck 1 is gone
Parameters Same hand-set rule every iteration Every stage has its own learned filters and nonlinearities The prior is no longer one formula; it is K different learned ones
What is learned Nothing Filters and influence functions, jointly, from data Earlier diffusion models fixed the filters and chose the diffusivity
Implementation while loop to a tolerance A fixed stack trained by back-propagation Structurally a CNN — and well-suited for parallel computation on GPUs
Performance WNNM 28.83 dB · 773 s 28.92 dB · 0.032 s (GPU) Best quality-per-second of the era
Limitation — Still one model per noise level Blind denoising remains unsolved
Keep this in mind for the next slide. DnCNN derives part of its own justification from a one-stage TNRD — the two are directly connected, not merely adjacent in time.
TNRD16 §1.2, §2, §3 · DnCNN17 Tables II, IV

DEEP CNN
DNCNN · 2017 · BEFORE → AFTER

DnCNN vs TNRD — remove the optimiser entirely

Zhang et al., IEEE TIP. TNRD unrolled the optimiser; DnCNN throws away the optimisation heritage and keeps only the network. The technical change is small, the consequence is the largest single step in this story.

The DnCNN architecture: Conv(+BN)+ReLU layers predict the residual noise, not the clean image. [DnCNN17 · Fig. 1]
Aspect TNRD (2016) DnCNN (2017) Why it matters
Core algorithm K diffusion stages, PDE-derived Plain deep CNN: Conv-BN-ReLU ×17, no pooling The architecture no longer has to resemble an optimiser at all
What the net outputs The restored image The noise — x = y − R(y) Residual learning: the 'do nothing' solution moves to zero, which is trivially reachable
Key enabler Learned influence functions Residual learning + batch normalisation, together Neither works nearly as well alone — the paper's most-cited empirical finding
Noise levels One model per σ DnCNN-B: one blind model, σ ∈ [0, 55] Drawback 4 solved; no noise estimate needed at test time
Performance 28.92 dB · 0.032 s 29.23 dB · 0.060 s (blind: 29.16) +0.6 dB over BM3D at all three noise levels
Applications Gaussian denoising One model for denoising + super-resolution + JPEG deblocking Redefine v and the same network solves three tasks
DnCNN17 §II-A, §III-A, §III-C, §III-D, Table II, Table IV · TNRD16

12
DEEP CNN
DNCNN · THE IMPLEMENTATION CHANGE

The innovation is eight characters

cszn/KAIR, models/network_dncnn.py, by DnCNN's own first author. The architecture is a list comprehension; the contribution is the return statement.

KAIR/models/network_dncnn.py — the whole network
m_head = B.conv(in_nc, nc, mode='C'+act_mode[-1])
m_body = [B.conv(nc, nc, mode='C'+act_mode)
          for _ in range(nb-2)]          # ← the entire network
m_tail = B.conv(nc, out_nc, mode='C')
 
def forward(self, x):
    n = self.model(x)
    return x-n                           # ← the contribution
 
# BEFORE (discriminative CNNs, ~2012-2016):
#     return self.model(x)      -> learn F(y) = x
# AFTER (DnCNN, 2017):
#     return x - self.model(x)  -> learn R(y) = v
  • Why that one change matters. From ResNet: a mapping close to the identity is hard to optimise. And y is much more like x than it is like v — so learning the image forces the network toward an identity transform, which seventeen ReLU layers have no natural way to express.
  • Learning the noise moves the trivial solution to zero, reachable by driving weights toward zero. Same function class, far easier optimisation landscape.
  • The synergy, in one sentence. Residual learning strips the image out of the hidden layers, making activations Gaussian-like and content-independent — which is exactly the regime batch-norm's batch statistics assume. Without residual learning, BN has a certain adverse effect on convergence.
  • Where the prior went. Nowhere in this file. It is in the .pth checkpoint this class will load. That is the moment the prior stopped being readable — and started being downloadable.
measured — cszn/KAIR, verbatim · DnCNN17 §II-A, §III-C

DEEP CNN
DNCNN · WHY IT WAS SOTA

What made it state of the art, and for how long

A SOTA claim with its qualifiers attached: the benchmark, and the margin measured against the ceiling the literature had already established.

+0.6 dB
over BM3D, all three σ

On BSD68. Prior work put the practical ceiling over BM3D at 0.3 dB and the estimated theoretical bound at 0.7 dB — so DnCNN took about 85% of the available headroom. [DnCNN17 §IV-B]

12 900×
faster than WNNM at 512²

773.2 s CPU → 0.060 s GPU. The device differs and the paper says so; the order of magnitude is the point. [DnCNN17 Table IV]

3 tasks
one model, one loss

DnCNN-3 handles denoising, super-resolution and JPEG deblocking by redefining v, beating a specialist baseline on all three. [DnCNN17 §III-D, Table V]

  • And it did it blind. DnCNN-B reaches 29.16 dB without being told σ, beating every noise-level-specific competitor in the table. That is drawback 4 closed.
  • Applications it opened: real-time denoising in imaging pipelines; the .pth checkpoint as a shippable artefact; and denoising as a reusable component — a trained denoiser can be dropped into variable-splitting solvers as a general-purpose prior. [SCUNet23 §1]
  • What it was not. On real sensor noise DnCNN was never the leader — it scores 23.66 dB on SIDD. That gap is slide 21's subject.
DnCNN17 §IV-B, Table II, Table IV · SCUNet23 §1

14
DEEP CNN
BOTTLENECKS 2 AND 3

What DnCNN broke, and the two bills it left

This slide is the hinge of the whole talk. Everything after it is the field paying off these two debts — and they were paid off by two different communities, independently, and never merged.

Bottleneck 2 — it needs clean data

  • The loss is ‖R(y) − (y − x)‖². It requires x.
  • For fluorescence microscopy, cryo-EM, MRI and astronomy a clean ground truth does not exist and cannot be acquired — you cannot photograph the same cell noiselessly.
  • So the most valuable applications of denoising were the ones DnCNN could not serve.
  • → Answered by the data branch. Presenter 2, slide 19.

Bottleneck 3 — it cannot see far enough

  • Receptive field is 35×35 pixels, chosen deliberately to match EPLL, the smallest effective patch size in the field. WNNM's is 361×361.
  • Visible in DnCNN's own Table III: on Barbara it loses to BM3D by 0.71 dB — the one Set12 image dominated by repetitive texture.
  • The paper explains it: repetitive images meet well with the non-local similarity prior that a 35×35 convolution stack cannot reach.
  • → Answered by the architecture branch. Presenter 2, slide 24.
A limitation visible in 2017, in the winning paper's own results table, that took until 2022 to fix. That is what an honest evolution story looks like.
DnCNN17 §III-A Eq. (1), Table I, Table III · N2V19 §1

15
HANDOVER · PRESENTER 2

2018: the field forks, and never merges

Two debts, two communities, two independent answers. Neither branch has adopted the other's advance — which is itself one of the findings of this project, and the source of the open problem we end on.

BRANCH A · BOTTLENECK 2

Change what the network is shown

Noise2Noise → Noise2Void → ZS-N2N → P2N. The architecture stays almost exactly where DnCNN left it; what moves is the training target. Each paper removes one more requirement until nothing is needed but the noisy image itself.

BRANCH B · BOTTLENECK 3

Change what the network is

Restormer, NAFNet, SCUNet, MambaIR. Supervision stays exactly as DnCNN had it — paired data, same loss family. What moves is the operator that replaces the 3×3 convolution.

THE EVIDENCE THEY NEVER MERGED

P2N ships the 2018 network

In the official P2N repository the class is literally named UNet_n2n_un, with the 2018 Noise2Noise channel widths. Seven years, and the backbone is unchanged. [measured]

THE OPEN QUESTION

Nobody has combined them

As far as we found, no published work trains a Transformer or state-space backbone under self-supervised RDC/DCS supervision. We return to this as a concrete proposal on slide 40.

DATA BRANCH
NOISE2NOISE · 2018 · BEFORE → AFTER

A theorem worth one conditional

Lehtinen et al., ICML 2018. The most striking ratio in this story: a substantial statistical result whose implementation change is a single branch on which tensor becomes the target.

Noise2Noise's own result: training on noisy targets (orange) tracks clean-target training (blue) almost exactly. [N2N18 · Fig. 1]
the change, in essence
# BEFORE — supervised (DnCNN, 2017)
target = clean                      # requires ground truth
loss   = mse(net(noisy), target)
 
# AFTER — Noise2Noise (2018)
target = second_noisy_shot          # ← the entire change
loss   = mse(net(noisy), target)
 
# network, optimiser, schedule, loss family: all unchanged
  • Why it works. L2 regression learns the conditional mean of the target. The paper states the consequence as a triviality: on expectation, the estimate remains unchanged if we replace the targets with random numbers whose expectations match the targets.
  • So a second noisy photograph of the same scene is a valid target, because the noise is zero-mean. Given infinite data the solution is identical to clean-target training; for finite data the extra variance shrinks with dataset size.
  • What it does NOT need: no likelihood model of the corruption, no density model of clean images.
  • Measured cost: 0.02 dB. Kodak/BSD300/Set14 at σ=25 — clean targets 31.63, noisy targets 31.61. The clean-data requirement was never actually necessary. [N2N18 Table 1]
N2N18 §2, Eq. (2)–(6), Table 1

DATA BRANCH
NOISE2VOID · 2019 · BEFORE → AFTER

N2V vs N2N — removing the second photograph

Krull et al., CVPR 2019. Noise2Noise still needs two independent shots of one scene, which rules out anything that moves and every archival image. N2V removes that too — and pays for it.

Traditional, Noise2Noise and Noise2Void training schemes side by side, with N2V's single-image blind-spot result on the right. [N2V19 · Fig. 1]
Aspect Noise2Noise (2018) Noise2Void (2019) Why it matters
Requires Two noisy shots per scene One noisy image. That is all. Applicable to any archive, any moving subject, any single acquisition
Key innovation Corrupted target with matching mean Blind-spot receptive field Prediction for pixel i uses its neighbourhood except pixel i
Why it cannot cheat Target is independent of input Noise is conditionally pixel-wise independent, so neighbours carry no information about nᵢ The identity solution becomes unreachable by construction
Implementation change Swap the target tensor Replace the centre pixel with a random neighbour; score the loss only there A masking trick, not an architecture — any standard CNN acquires the property
Performance (BSD68 σ=25) 28.86 dB 27.71 dB −1.15 dB, and 0.88 dB below BM3D — the cost is real and the paper does not hide it
Applications Burst photography, rendering Cryo-TEM, fluorescence microscopy, cell tracking Domains where the paper's own figure captions the ground truth column does not exist
The honest framing, and the one to use if challenged. Self-supervision is not a quality technique, it is an availability technique. Where clean data exists, supervision wins by 1.35 dB. Where it does not, the comparison is not 27.71 against 29.23 — it is 27.71 against nothing at all.
N2V19 §3.1, §3.4, §3.5, §4.1, Fig. 4 · N2N18 Table 1
20072014201720222025

DATA BRANCH
ZS-N2N · 2023 · P2N · 2025

Down to one image, then down to no sacrifice

The branch finishes by removing the last two requirements. Compressed into one slide because the pattern is now familiar — each paper removes exactly one thing.

The information-lossy barrier made visible: ZS-N2N, MASH and ATBSN all lose fine structure that P2N's renoise-and-agree supervision keeps. [P2N25 · Fig. 2]
ZS-N2N (2023) P2N (2025)
Requirement removed The training set. No corpus, no pretraining. The information loss itself.
Key innovation A pair downsampler: two fixed diagonal filters split one image into a noisy pair with similar signal and independent noise. RDC — renoise the model's own output with + and −, giving y⁺ and y⁻ at full resolution. DCS — train the two denoised results to agree.
Implementation change Two fixed stride-2 convolutions; a 20 000-parameter two-layer net fitted to that one image; residual + consistency loss. Three forward passes per step, on tensors that do not exist until the model has run once. Output compared against output, not against a target.
Why it is not just a new loss It is a new input construction. Same: a loss scores a fixed prediction against a fixed target. P2N changes what goes in, how many passes, and which pair is compared.
Cost paid Half the spatial resolution during training; 1–2 K gradient steps per image. Three passes per step; still per-image test-time optimisation.
Applications Single archival images, one-off scientific captures; ~1 min on CPU vs Self2Self's 1.2 h on GPU. Self-supervised denoising where masking artefacts are unacceptable.
The through-line: the network never moved, the target did. Clean image (2018) → second copy (2019) → training set (2023) → information loss (2025). Four papers, four requirements removed, one U-Net throughout.
ZS-N2N23 §3, §4 · P2N25 (CVPR 2025) · repository measured

ARCHITECTURE
BOTTLENECK 3 · THE RECEIPT

One number proves the receptive field is the problem

Identical models, identical table, identical noise level. The only thing that changes is the dataset — and the gain changes by a factor of five.

Effective receptive field: CNNs stay tightly local, Transformers spread further, the Mamba-based backbone activates the widest field. [MambaIR24 · Fig. 1]
+0.39 dB
BSD68, σ=50 · DnCNN → Restormer

Ordinary natural images, little long-range repetition. Five years of architecture research buys almost nothing.

+1.98 dB
Urban100, σ=50 · same two models

Photographs of buildings — windows and railings repeating across hundreds of pixels. Five times the gain, on the dataset made of repetition.

−0.71 dB
Barbara, σ=25 · DnCNN vs BM3D, 2017

The same phenomenon, visible five years earlier in DnCNN's own results, on the one Set12 image dominated by repetitive texture.

  • What this proves. The architecture branch did not make denoising uniformly better. It made denoising better specifically where non-locality matters — which is exactly the capability a 3×3 convolution stack structurally lacks.
  • Why depth cannot fix it. Receptive field grows linearly with depth: (2d+1)². Reaching WNNM's 361×361 the DnCNN way needs about 180 layers. The fix had to be a different operator, not more of the same one.
Provenance: the 0.39-versus-1.98 comparison is our own analysis of published values, both taken from Restormer's Table 4 so the protocol is identical. Say computed from Table 4 if challenged.
Restormer22 Table 4 · DnCNN17 Table III, Table I

ARCHITECTURE
RESTORMER · 2022 · BEFORE → AFTER

Attention becomes affordable by changing one axis

Zamir et al., CVPR 2022. Standard self-attention costs O(W²H²) — a 256×256 image needs a 4.3-billion-entry attention matrix, against 196 tokens for a ViT. Restormer's innovation is to attend over channels instead of pixels.

Restormer/basicsr/models/archs/restormer_arch.py — Attention.forward
# BEFORE — spatial attention (ViT / SwinIR)
#   'b c h w -> b head (h w) c'      -> q@kT is (HW x HW)
#   256x256  ->  65,536 x 65,536
 
# AFTER — Restormer MDTA
q = rearrange(q,'b (head c) h w -> b head c (h w)',
              head=self.num_heads)   # ← pixels on the LAST axis
k = rearrange(k, ...); v = rearrange(v, ...)
q = F.normalize(q,dim=-1); k = F.normalize(k,dim=-1)
attn = (q @ k.transpose(-2,-1)) * self.temperature
#   -> (C/head x C/head).  At level 1: 48 x 48, any image size
  • One einops pattern is the entire complexity claim. Putting pixels on the last axis makes q @ k.transpose(-2,-1) a C×C matrix — 48×48 whether the image is 256² or 4000×3000. Cost becomes linear in pixels.
  • Is it really global? Honestly: not pairwise-pixel. Every channel is computed from every pixel, so channel statistics carry image-wide information; the paper says global relationships are implicitly modelled and never claims otherwise.
  • The depth-wise convolutions are load-bearing, not decoration. Removing qkv_dwconv costs 0.15 dB on Urban100 σ=50 — more than most architecture papers gain in total. [Restormer22 Table 7]
  • Why SOTA: first method past 40 dB on both SIDD and DND; leads Urban100 at every noise level; 3.14× fewer FLOPs and 13× faster than SwinIR. Published at CVPR 2022; how long it holds those tables is not something any source states.

ARCHITECTURE
NAFNET · 2022 · BEFORE → AFTER

The paper that asked whether any of it was necessary

Chen et al., ECCV 2022. While everyone added mechanisms, NAFNet removed them and scored higher. Its derivation is the most elegant reasoning in the modern half of this story.

The lineage NAFNet derives in one figure: the transformer block simplified step by step down to SimpleGate and SCA. [NAFNet22 · Fig. 3]
NAFNet/basicsr/models/archs/NAFNet_arch.py
# BEFORE — GELU, then a gate
#   GELU(x) = 0.5x(1+tanh[sqrt(2/pi)(x+0.044715x^3)])
#   CA(X)   = X * sigmoid(W2 relu(W1 pool(X)))
 
# AFTER — SimpleGate: the gate IS the nonlinearity
def forward(self, x):
    x1, x2 = x.chunk(2, dim=1)
    return x1 * x2                # ← replaces GELU entirely
 
# AFTER — SCA: no sigmoid, no relu
self.sca = nn.Sequential(nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
                         nn.Conv2d(c, c, 1))
  • The derivation. GELU is a special case of a gated linear unit with f, g = identity and σ = Φ. But a GLU itself contains nonlinearity and does not depend on σ — f(X)⊙g(X) is nonlinear because a product of two linear maps is not linear. So delete the activation; the gate already supplies it.
  • Apply the same argument to channel attention and both its nonlinearities vanish too. Result: no Sigmoid, no ReLU, no GELU, no Softmax anywhere — the first work demonstrating that the nonlinear activation functions may not be necessary for SOTA computer vision methods.
  • Both simplifications improved the score. SimpleGate beats GELU (+0.08), SCA beats CA (+0.03) on SIDD.
  • The uncomfortable finding in their own ablation: the largest single gain is LayerNorm, +0.44 dB — because it stabilises training at a 10× larger learning rate. A large share of reported architectural progress in restoration is optimisation progress wearing a costume.
Why SOTA: 40.30 dB on SIDD — the highest real-noise result in our comparison — at less than half the previous best's compute. Published at ECCV 2022. And by far the simplest code to maintain.

ARCHITECTURE
SCUNET · 2023 · MAMBAIR · 2024

Two more answers — one architectural, one not about architecture at all

The branch does not end with Transformers. MambaIR proposes a different operator again; SCUNet argues the operator was never the problem.

The Swin-Conv-UNet pipeline: swin-conv blocks combine local and non-local modelling on the way down and back up a UNet backbone. [SCUNet23 · Fig. 1]
MambaIR (2024) SCUNet (2023)
The claim Attention is quadratic; windowing surrenders globality. Borrow a selective state-space model — global receptive field at linear cost. The benchmark is the problem. A model trained on AWGN performs poorly for most of real images due to noise assumption mismatch.
Technical change S6 recurrence with input-dependent B, C, Δ. Dual form: recurrent (unbounded memory) for reach, convolutional for parallel training. Keep local and non-local priors in parallel — split the feature map, half to a Swin block, half to a residual conv block.
Implementation change Flatten the image to a sequence; four-directional scan; add a local conv (fixes local pixel forgetting) and channel attention (fixes redundancy). The dataloader becomes the contribution: Gaussian, Poisson, speckle, JPEG, and sensor noise synthesised through a real inverted ISP, plus resizing and double degradation.
Why SOTA / where Best DND result, 40.04 dB — by 0.01 dB. Leads super-resolution on Manga109 ×2 by 0.41 dB over SwinIR. Not top of any AWGN table — and does not need to be. 9.663 M parameters, smallest of the four, built to survive real photographs.
Cost / limitation Will not import without compiled CUDA extensions. Its own changelog records that published thop complexity figures were wrong. [measured] Its abstract still concedes a general-purpose blind real denoiser remains unsolved.

WHY SEVERAL SOTAS

Four reasons the field has not converged on one method

This is the question the professor is most likely to ask, so it gets its own slide rather than a sentence.

REASON 1

The benchmarks measure different things

BSD68 measures average-case Gaussian removal and has saturated — 0.36 dB across five years. Urban100 measures long-range self-similarity. SIDD and DND measure real sensor noise. A method can lead one and trail another without any contradiction.

REASON 2

The cost axes disagree with each other

Our own measurements give three incompatible rankings of the same models: by parameters DnCNN wins; by CPU wall-clock the P2N backbone wins; by real-noise quality NAFNet wins. NAFNet has 4.4× Restormer's parameters and runs 5.5× faster. 'More efficient' is meaningless without naming the metric and the device.

REASON 3

Deployment constraints are not quality constraints

MambaIR leads DND by 0.01 dB and cannot be imported without compiled CUDA extensions. SCUNet leads nothing and is a third of Restormer's size. Which one is 'best' depends entirely on what you are shipping onto what hardware.

REASON 4

Supervision availability partitions the field

Branch A and branch B answer different questions. Where clean pairs exist, supervision wins by 1.35 dB. Where they do not, the self-supervised methods are not worse — they are the only option, and the supervised SOTA is simply unavailable.

APPLICATIONS AND TRADE-OFFS

What you would actually deploy, and why

The honest answer to 'which is best' names the constraint first. Five constraints, five different answers, all current — which is what an unresolved research question looks like when you have to ship something.

If your constraint is… Deploy Because Accept
Real photos, GPU, paired data NAFNet 40.30 dB on SIDD; best accuracy-per-millisecond we measured; simplest code to maintain 116 M parameters
Repetitive structure, max quality Restormer Leads Urban100 at every σ; only method past 40 dB on both real-noise benchmarks 10.4 s per 256² on CPU
CPU or memory bound SCUNet 9.7 M parameters; synthetic-degradation training survives resized and JPEG'd input Not top of any AWGN table
No clean data exists at all P2N / ZS-N2N Microscopy, cryo-EM, astronomy — where ground truth cannot be acquired Per-image test-time optimisation
No data, no GPU, no dependencies BM3D Seventeen years old and still beats AWGN-trained DnCNN on real noise by 1.99 dB 2.85 s, and a quality ceiling
Denoising is rarely the product. It is preprocessing for detection and segmentation, a plug-and-play prior inside deblurring and super-resolution solvers, and — per DnCNN-3 — a template: redefine v and the same network does super-resolution and JPEG deblocking. [SCUNet23 §1 · DnCNN17 §III-D]

OPEN PROBLEMS

What eighteen years did not solve

Each of these is grounded in a documented limitation from the papers themselves or in our own measurements — not speculation.

OPEN 1

A blind denoiser for real cameras

SCUNet's abstract states it remains unsolved. Neither synthetic degradation nor SIDD-trained models generalise to an unseen camera with an unseen ISP, and no benchmark currently measures that. DnCNN scores 23.66 dB on SIDD — a 16 dB collapse, not a graceful degradation.

OPEN 2

Fidelity metrics reward blur

Every loss in the modern field is L1, L2 or PSNR, and all three recover a conditional mean — which is smoother than any plausible clean image. Noise2Noise names the mechanism itself: L2 training results in spatial blurriness. While leaderboards rank by PSNR, the incentive points the wrong way.

OPEN 3

Nobody agrees what 'efficient' means

Three incompatible rankings from our own measurements, and MambaIR's changelog concedes its published complexity figures were wrong. Efficiency claims across papers are close to uncheckable.

OPEN 4

The benchmarks have saturated

BSD68 σ=25 moved 0.36 dB in five years while Urban100 moved five times as much and SIDD moved sixteen decibels. A benchmark that cannot distinguish 2017 from 2022 is no longer measuring what the field works on.

PROPOSAL DIRECTIONS

Four research directions the limitations actually justify

Each is tied to a specific documented gap, states what would change, and names how it would be measured. None of these claims a paper achieved something it did not.

Direction Grounded in What would change How you would measure it
Cross the fork: self-supervised supervision on a modern backbone Our own finding — no published work trains a Transformer or SSM backbone under RDC/DCS supervision; P2N still ships the 2018 U-Net Replace UNet_n2n_un with a Restormer or NAFNet block under P2N's RDC/DCS training signal N2V's own protocol on BSD68 σ=25 and on the cryo-TEM / CTC sets; does the 1.35 dB self-supervision gap shrink?
Cross-ISP generalisation benchmark SCUNet's abstract: a general blind real denoiser remains unsolved, and no benchmark tests unseen cameras Train on SIDD, evaluate on DND and a held-out camera; report the drop as the headline number Δ PSNR between seen and unseen ISP — a metric nobody currently reports
Perceptual objective without losing fidelity Noise2Noise names L2's spatial blurriness; perceptual losses are common in SR and absent from denoising Add an LPIPS or no-reference term to NAFNet's PSNR loss and report both axes, not one PSNR and LPIPS jointly on SIDD — accept a small dB loss for a measured perceptual gain
An efficiency protocol the field can agree on Three incompatible rankings from our measurements; MambaIR's corrected thop figures Report parameters, MACs and wall-clock on a named device, with the counting method stated Reproduce the table across CPU and GPU; the ratio changes are themselves the result
The first row is the one we would pursue. It falls directly out of the structural claim of this project — the two branches have never merged — and it is cheap to test, because both halves already exist as working code.

31
CONCLUSION

The evolution, in one paragraph

Denoising is the cleanest case study in how computer vision replaced hand-designed priors with learned ones, because here the prior is written down explicitly and you can watch it move.

Four eras, three bottlenecks. Manual prior design ended when DnCNN made the prior a downloadable file. That created two new debts — it needed clean data, and it could only see 35 pixels — and in 2018 the field forked to pay them off separately.

Neither branch has adopted the other's advance. And because three architectures now lead three different benchmarks while none solves real-camera generalisation, the story ends in an open question rather than a winner.

— What the evidence in this talk supports.

BACKUP · QUESTION INDEX

Where to find the answer to what you are about to be asked

Kept for the Q&A. The full evidence for every claim in this talk is in the 100-slide master deck, indexed here by the question likely to prompt it.

If asked… Answer in one line Master deck
Why is 0.6 dB a big deal? Practical ceiling over BM3D was 0.3 dB, theoretical bound 0.7 dB — DnCNN took 85% 10, 37
Why predict noise, not the image? y is closer to x than to v, so learning the image forces an identity mapping — the hard point in parameter space 33
Why do RL and BN need each other? RL makes layer inputs Gaussian-like and content-independent — what BN's batch statistics assume 34
Why depth 17? RF = (2d+1)² set to 35×35 to match EPLL, the smallest effective patch size in the field 35
How can noisy targets work? L2 learns the conditional mean; the mean of a zero-mean corrupted target is the clean target 43
Where is Restormer's attention linear? Attention.forward — the rearrange puts pixels last, so q@kᵀ is C×C not HW×HW 69
Why is NAFNet faster with more parameters? 1×1 and depth-wise convs hit optimised GEMM paths; rearrange forces tensor-layout changes 77
What did the code tell you that the papers did not? Padding constants differ 8×; SPI cuts parameters and triples latency; MambaIR needs CUDA to import 75, 77
Which would you deploy? Name the constraint first — five constraints, five answers, all current 89
Did you verify the PSNRs yourself? No. Every quality figure is reproduced from a named published table; only parameters and latency are ours 81, 93
